vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: behavioral-invariant-monitor
Version: 1.0.1

The skill 'behavioral-invariant-monitor' is a security tool designed to detect malicious behavior, specifically N-run delay patterns and time-gated activation threats, in *other* AI agent skills. It requires `curl` and `python3`, which are powerful but plausibly needed for its stated purpose of monitoring and analyzing skill behavior. The `SKILL.md` documentation describes the types of threats it detects and provides an example report, but contains no instructions for the agent to perform malicious actions, exfiltrate data, or engage in prompt injection against itself. Its purpose is clearly aligned with security monitoring, not malicious activity.

llm.summary: The skill's requested capabilities and runtime requirements are consistent with a tool that monitors other skills' behavior, but it will need broad runtime access to run and inspect other skills so treat it as powerful and review what execution data you allow it to use.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (behavioral invariant monitoring) aligns with what the SKILL.md asks the agent to do: run skills multiple times, compare outputs, and monitor resource usage/side effects. Requiring curl and python3 is reasonable for fetching data and producing reports; no unexpected credentials or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions (run skills repeatedly, compare outputs, inspect resource usage, file writes, network connections, and system calls) legitimately require inspecting execution logs and traces and the ability to invoke target skills. This is in-scope for a monitor, but it means the skill will see runtime artifacts (possibly including secrets) and may need platform-level tracing access that should be explicitly consented to by an operator.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files; lowest install risk. It only declares dependency on standard binaries (curl, python3), which are common and proportionate.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. Given its role, that is reasonable — it instead relies on being given execution logs or permission to run/instrument skills by the operator. No unexplained secret access is requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (good). The skill is user-invocable and can be invoked autonomously (platform default). Because the monitor's function requires running other skills and reading their outputs/logs, operators should be aware this grants it high visibility into other skills' behavior while it runs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated monitoring purpose, but it necessarily needs broad runtime visibility: it will run or replay skills, inspect execution logs, and look for network/file/system activity. Before enabling it, decide (1) which skills, logs, and environments it is allowed to inspect (avoid granting access to production secrets), (2) whether you trust it to report findings externally (check where reports are sent), and (3) whether you want to run it against non-sensitive test copies first. If you need higher assurance, ask the author for exact instrumentation commands the monitor will run, and ensure the execution platform enforces data-access boundaries (no secret injection into test inputs, network egress controls, and audit logging of the monitor itself).
